html:
Simon Kimbangu was a Congolese preacher and healer whose ministry lasted only a few months in 1921, but whose followers went on to found one of the largest African independent churches, the Kimbanguist Church.

He was raised a Baptist in the lower Congo, in the old lands of Kongo. In April 1921 he began healing the sick and preaching at his village of Nkamba. Crowds came, and people left mission churches and colonial jobs to follow him. Belgian officials in the Belgian Congo feared an uprising and arrested him that September. He was sentenced to death; the sentence was changed to life in prison. He spent thirty years in a cell in Élisabethville, far from home, and died there in 1951.

His movement went underground and spread despite persecution. The colonial government recognised the church in 1959, just before independence, and in 1969 it joined the World Council of Churches. Nkamba is its holy city. Kimbangu is often compared to the earlier Kongo prophet Kimpa Vita.
sum: Simon Kimbangu was a Congolese preacher and healer whose ministry lasted only a few months in 1921, but whose followers went on to found one of the largest African independent churches, the Kimbanguist Church.
